chart.title: Weed severity by species, % of samples

rows.label: weeds_recommendation
cells: A herbicide application is recommended. This field should be prioritized for herbicide application.

rows.label: weeds_agent
cells: Western weed pressure correlates with poorer emergence and drainage: 0.0398 avg severity with 93-97% emergence and 8.5-9.6% skips on 100% poor/moderate soils vs 0.00067, 101%, and 6.7% in the northeast. May 23rd-June 14th was wetter/warmer than normal (131.5 mm, 22.3°C), associated with the June 1st spike.

Weed pressure peaked on June 1st (avg severity 0.1908, affected 100%) and fell by July 3rd (0.00034, 19.4%), associated with the crop staying at 100.8% emergence and V13-V16. No meaningful within-field correlation was found because only one northeastern region was present.
Agentic correlation analysis was not performed. Last scouting passes showed consistently clean readings with no significant variation or change to investigate.

Weeds correlate with slightly poorer establishment in the northeastern region: emergence averaged 98.0% and skip rate 8.76% in low-weed zones vs 100.9% and 6.63% where weeds were absent. They also correlate with a wetter soil mix, with 58.3% somewhat poorly drained vs 28.9% in the no-weed area.

rows.label: nutrients_agent
cells: Nutrient deficiencies correlate most with the northwestern, somewhat poorly drained zone: avg severity 0.275 vs 0.238-0.247 in the moderately well drained SW/E, and N appeared only in NW at 0.0465. No meaningful correlation showed with disease or stage, since all regions were V6-V12 and disease was 0.0.

Northeastern nutrient deficiencies correlate with 71% moderately well drained and 29% somewhat poorly drained soils, with avg severity 0.5005 and 47.8% affected vs ~0 in the southeast. They were at V13-V16, and May 16th's 74.4 mm rain plus June 6th's 37.0 mm rain are associated with uptake stress.

Nutrient deficiencies correlate with moderately well/somewhat poorly drained soils in the southwestern and northeastern regions, with avg severity 0.284 vs 0.000 in the southeastern no-deficiency zone. Severity rose from 0.037 on June 14th to 0.338 on July 3rd, and N detections expanded after June 6th rain and during the July 10th-20th drought.

High deficiencies correlate with moderately well drained, group C soils in the southwestern and northeastern regions: avg severity 0.366 vs 0.000004 and affected 25.6% vs 0.0%. Severity spikes on July 3rd (0.426; 40.3%) and August 6th (0.366; 25.6%), with S then N dominance after the July 10th-21st drought/heat.

rows.label: diseases_agent
cells: Agentic correlation analysis was not performed. Last scouting passes showed consistently clean readings with no significant variation or change to investigate.

Disease pressure is concentrated in the southwestern region, with avg severity 0.3748 vs 0.000005 in the northeastern region on July 3rd; it rose from 0.0 on June 14th to 30.67% affected. Warm, wet periods (262.2 mm rain, 74.4 mm on May 16th) are associated with this buildup.

Disease pressure was absent in the northeastern region (0.0 avg severity on July 20th; 2.7% affected on July 3rd), so no meaningful correlation was found. The only co-located nutrient deficiency signal was minimal at 1.5% affected, which does not support a robust link.
Agentic correlation analysis was not performed. Last scouting passes showed consistently clean readings with no significant variation or change to investigate.
